evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor: 11.17 mg/L at t=49 h falling to 4.12 mg/L at t=52 h; 5 of last 6 readings below 5.2 mg/L
Source batches source-1/2/3 never record DO below ~7.4 mg/L over 0-96 h, confirming the receiving event is anomalous (estimated transfer multiplier ~0.52 at t=50 h)
Forward model: keep/increase_air/reduce_feed/combined all predict post-decision minimum DO 1.35-1.64 mg/L with 2.8-5.4 h below the 2 mg/L limit
Forward model: strong_feed_reduction predicts minimum DO 2.58 mg/L, 0 h below limit, 255.9 kg product mass (highest of all actions), 4/5 sensitivity members feasible
submission.rationale: At t=50 h the receiving fermenter suffered an abrupt oxygen-transfer collapse (DO fell from ~11 mg/L to ~4.1 mg/L within 2 h; model-estimated transfer multiplier 0.52), unlike any source batch. Forward-model evaluation shows keep, increase_air, reduce_feed, and combined all centrally violate the 2 mg/L DO hard constraint post-decision (min DO 1.35-1.64 mg/L, 2.8-5.4 h below limit), so they are not justifiable even though some sensitivity members look favorable. Only strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6 + air x1.15) is centrally feasible: min DO 2.58 mg/L, zero below-limit hours, and it retains the greatest product mass (~256 kg), since cutting oxygen demand more than offsets the growth-rate penalty. Stop is unwarranted because a supported feasible operating plan exists.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is a source-calibrated approximation, not the hidden receiving realization; the strong_feed_reduction plan is feasible in 4/5 assumed sensitivity members but not all (range 1.31-3.33 mg/L), and the estimate of the t=50 h transfer collapse depends on the recent online DO readings. A worst-case mismatch could push DO below 2 mg/L; monitoring post-intervention DO is essential, but the nominal margin (~0.58 mg/L) plus feed reduction gives the best-supported feasible option among those available.
